title: Opt-in session reminders (D39): the setting off and on
note: Both arms are bake-rs at c8f7aa9223; the on arm sets `schedules: true` through EVAL_SETTINGS_ON. The setting is off by default and the default model surface is unchanged from develop (the first-request fixtures are identical), so this record measures what turning it on costs. On the opt-in reminder scenario every on sample called schedule_create once and wrote the returned id, 21/21; without the setting there is no schedule tool, so every off sample fails the predicate, which requires a schedule_create call. Those failures are the point of the comparison, not regressions. The flagged total-token rises, 17 to 27% on every model, come from about 1.9 KB of tool definitions in every request (toolSchemaChars 4.1-4.3k to 6.0-6.2k), with no change in standard-suite failures; that is the cost of the opt-in, and the reason it stays off by default. The gemini-3.8-flash-high tool errors, 0 to 2, are a failing node test.cjs before the fix and git run outside a repository in path_discovery, unrelated to the schedule tools. The first run stopped at the 5M-token limit after 360 of 378 samples, since off reminder samples search at length for a tool they lack; deepseek-v4-pro's trial 2 comes from a second run of the same binary (sha256 9aa4aee7e3c77479…, built at 41f1388d9c, which changes only scripts/release), keeping only its trial-2 samples.

settings.effort: each route's effort is in routes: medium by default, DeepSeek high (it has no medium), and an EVAL_MODELS @<effort> replaces either

regressionRule: all tasks, per model: total tokens with the 95% interval above zero; requests up more than 10% with the 95% interval above zero; failures +2 or more; any tool-error increase
